text.p: German airline Eurowings Luftverkehrs AG said it would show improved 1996 profits and forecast double-figure growth in passengers and turnover this year.
Eurowings chairman Reinhard Santner said the privately-owned carrier expected a 15 percent rise to 2.2 million passengers and a 22 percent rise to 560 million marks turnover this year.
The airline improved turnover 14 percent to 460 million marks last year and increased passenger numbers 4.6 percent to 1.88 million, he added.
"We had a very positive year and the profit was substantially better than 1995," Santner told Reuters in an interview at the ITB travel fair in Berlin this week.
The airline made a group net profit of 2.1 million marks on a turnover of 410 million marks in 1995 following a loss of eight million marks in 1994.
Code-share flights with KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and Air France would be expanded over the course of the year, Santer said.
Eurowings now operated 23 daily flights on nine routes from Germany to Amsterdam in co-operation with KLM and was the second-largest foreign airline at Schipol Airport, he added.
Eurowings would use two new 142-seat Airbus A319s for summer charter flights for German tour operators to Mediterranean destinations.
Sales revenue from charter flights should rise to about 95 million marks from 53 million marks last year, Santner added.
Eurowings marketing manager Ulrich Sigman said the airline would expand ticketless flying on several domestic routes later this year.
But there were no short-term plans for Internet sales or large-scale telephone sales, he added.
